core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex representing E with injective terms, and use preservation of K-injectivity under restriction to an open to conclude that the derived pushforwards along U, V and U cap V are computed by the corresponding pushforwards of the restrictions (proof lines 8134-8141).
Identify the sought distinguished triangle with the one attached to the displayed short exact sequence of complexes of sections (proof lines 8141-8153).

Verify exactness of that sequence of complexes termwise: for every open W and every degree the sequence of values over W, W cap U, W cap V and W cap U cap V is exact, which is the combinatorial statement used in the Mayer-Vietoris lemma (proof lines 8154-8163).
proof_roadmap: Represent E by a K-injective complex with injective terms (proof lines 8134-8141).
Recognise the triangle as one attached to a short exact sequence (proof lines 8141-8153).
difficulty_reason: For a ringed space X which is the union of two open subspaces U and V, the lemma produces a distinguished triangle relating an arbitrary object E of the derived category to the derived pushforwards of its restrictions to U, V and the intersection (statement lines 8118-8131). The proof chooses a K-injective representative whose terms are injective modules, so that the derived pushforwards along the three open inclusions are computed by the corresponding pushforwards of the restricted complexes; this reduces the statement to the distinguished triangle associated to a short exact sequence of complexes (proof lines 8133-8153). The remaining point is exactness of that sequence of complexes, which is checked termwise: for every open W and every degree n the sequence of sections over W, W cap U, W cap V and W cap U cap V is exact, exactly the combinatorial statement used in the Mayer-Vietoris proof (proof lines 8154-8163). The claim is H2: one adjunction-free reduction plus a termwise exactness check, with no step left to the reader beyond the cited exactness.
